Smart Mars Exploration Map is a proposed interactive tool designed to help future astronauts plan and carry out safer Marswalks. It brings together data from multiple NASA missions in one layered map, including surface images, terrain and elevation, potential hazards, and locations of scientific interest.

Explorers can use the map to review a proposed route, identify areas that may be difficult to cross, and examine available environmental observations with their dates.

Our project addresses the challenge by making complex Mars data easier to understand and use in one place. It is important because better planning can help astronauts manage risks, use their mission time effectively, and discover promising locations for scientific research.
details:
Project Details

Smart Mars Exploration Map is a proposed interactive tool designed to help astronauts plan and conduct Marswalks. It brings together information from multiple NASA science missions to create a layered view of a selected location or route on Mars.

How It Works

The map is designed to let users explore a selected area and view different layers of information, including surface images, elevation, terrain features, potential hazards, and scientific points of interest. Users can plan a route from a starting point to a destination and review important features along the way.

Available environmental observations can also be displayed with their dates, helping users understand when the information was collected.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to make Mars mission data easier to understand and use. By bringing route information, possible hazards, and scientific locations together, it can help astronauts prepare for their journeys and make informed decisions.

The intended impact is to support safer exploration, make effective use of mission time, and help astronauts identify promising locations for scientific research and sample collection.

Proposed Tools and Technology

The project could be developed as a web-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, together with a mapping library and publicly available NASA mission datasets. A computer and internet connection could be used to develop the application and access the data.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative idea is to connect exploration, safety, and science in one interactive map. Instead of viewing mission data separately, users can examine how the terrain, a proposed route, and scientific locations relate to one another.

The team considered several factors, including ease of use, clear presentation, potential route hazards, scientific value, and the availability and age of the data.
